checks.name: Runs test (is the sequence random?)
checks.detail: 14,561 runs vs 14,050 expected (z = +6.10, p = 0.000): more switches than chance: results tend to alternate. Check that it also holds out of sample.

checks.name: Does one result predict the next?
checks.detail: lag-1 correlation -0.0364 (z = -6.11). Statistically non-zero, but check its size: a correlation this small moves the next window's odds by only about 1.8 percentage points, less than fees cost.

checks.name: Hour-of-day lean holds out of sample?
checks.detail: Split at 2026-06-06. Hours that looked significant in the first half: 13:00; still significant, same direction, in the second half: none. Correlation of hourly leans between halves: -0.13 (near zero: the hourly pattern is noise).

checks.name: Streak behaviour holds out of sample?
checks.detail: after 3 Ups the next was Up 46.0% (first half, n=1,524) vs 47.9% (second half, n=1,664); after 3 Downs the next was Up 53.6% (first half, n=1,567) vs 53.3% (second half, n=1,594). For a fade-or-follow rule to pay, the same lean must show in both halves and be larger than the ~2–3¢ per contract that spread and fees cost.

checks.name: Kalshi price edge holds out of sample?
checks.detail: 2 price levels looked clearly profitable in the first half (buy No at 30–40¢, buy Yes at 70–80¢) but did not hold up in the second. 6 more showed a paper profit that sits inside its error band, so it could just be luck: buy Yes at 20–30¢: +10.4¢ ±13.8 (n=49); buy No at 40–50¢: +7.8¢ ±13.8 (n=49); buy Yes at 10–20¢: +6.9¢ ±9.1 (n=86). Most windows trade under 10¢ or over 90¢; there, recent results ran -1.1¢ to +0.6¢ per contract.

checks.name: Chance findings to expect
checks.detail: The report tests 35 hour, weekday and slot groups; at 95% confidence about 1.8 would look significant by luck alone. Found: 0. That's no more than luck would produce.
